recentItems.title: Live: Latest in Middle East as the situation remains unclear
recentItems.description: Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon, according to the Lebanese health ministry, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within areas occupied by its troops. The foreign ministers of Egypt, Qatar, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Indonesia and Pakistan on Sunday strongly condemned remarks by two Israeli ministers concerning the displacement of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, as the situation in Middle East remains unclear.

recentItems.title: China's private space companies set their sights on the moon
recentItems.description:
In China, private space companies are getting ready to go lunar.

At the International Deep Space Exploration Conference this week in Hefei, capital of Anhui Province, companies showcased plans for lunar exploration – from robots to rovers to new rockets built for deeper space missions.

recentItems.title: UN Resident Coordinator summarizes key factors behind China's air quality gains
recentItems.description:
Stephen Jackson, UN Resident Coordinator in China, praised the country's remarkable achievements in air quality improvement, attributing them to four key drivers: strong political will, technological innovation, advanced data monitoring and regional cooperation. He highlighted China's successful domestic practices as valuable experiences in tackling air pollution and called for extraordinary global cooperation to advance clean air initiatives worldwide.#GoodPoint

recentItems.title: Predicting the unpredictable: Living on a fault line
recentItems.description:
Italy sits on the boundary where the African tectonic plate dives down beneath the Eurasian plate. It makes it one of the most seismically active countries in Europe, but despite widespread scientific advancements, earthquakes continue to devastate communities, raising the question: Can we really ever predict earthquakes? 

To understand the reality for many Italians, RAZOR's Gabrielle Lawrence heads to Campi Flegrei, near Naples and in the shadow of Vesuvius, one of Italy's most seismically active regions. Since 2018, unrest has intensified, with multiple magnitude-4 earthquakes in 2025 and persistent ground uplift threatening hundreds of thousands of residents. We meet Professor Marzocchi and Dr. Tramelli at the Pisciarelli Fumarole, the area's largest volcanic vent. The National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV), in collaboration with Stanford University, is now using artificial intelligence to analyze vast seismic datasets to understand the complex volcanic system.

Pavia, in northern Italy, is another seismic hotspot and one of Europe's leading earthquake engineering laboratories. Here, researchers operate experimental shake tables capable of recreating devastating seismic forces. Full-scale buildings are violently tested to understand exactly how structures fail — we ask engineers how future cities can be built to survive.

RAZOR has also been given special access to the nerve center of Italian seismology – the operations rooms of the National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) in Rome. When an earthquake occurs anywhere in the country, it appears in real time on screens here.
